changes.before: Replace puts badge.label with puts badge.decorate. What happens?
changes.after: A private method can help other methods inside a class without being an ordinary outside entry point.

before: Methods are normally public. private changes the default visibility of subsequent instance method definitions. decorate is an internal helper; label can call it without an explicit receiver.

An outside caller cannot use badge.decorate as a public method call. Visibility organizes an API, not a security sandbox: reflective operations can bypass some visibility restrictions. Ruby also has protected methods for restricted receiver calls within the class family; they are not public either.

Complete local Ruby example; the app itself does not execute it:
```ruby
class Badge
  def label
    decorate
  end
  private
  def decorate
    "[ready]"
  end
end
badge = Badge.new
puts badge.label
```
Expected output or behavior: [ready]. Compiler evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.
